current_episode.title: Joe Lewandowski, McCarthy PM on BJC Campus Renewal Phase 3

guest.bio_context: Lewandowski has been with McCarthy Building Company since 2005 and has dedicated his entire professional career to healthcare construction across the country. He managed the New Orleans VA Medical Center replacement project from 2013 to 2016, a billion-dollar campus that replaced critical medical infrastructure damaged by Hurricane Katrina. He is currently leading the construction team on Phase 3 of the BJC Healthcare Campus Renewal Project.

context.real_quote: We not only take pride in building for BJC, who's a national leader among health care organizations, but also feel special to be building a hospital that's so important to the people in and around St. Louis.

pending_qa.q: How did the COVID-19 pandemic impact the timeline of a major healthcare campus construction project?
pending_qa.r: McCarthy was brought onto the project in December 2019 for design and pre-construction services. The pandemic caused BJC leadership to pause the project for evaluation, resulting in approximately a nine-month delay. The project was originally scheduled to start in spring 2021 but was rescheduled to begin in November 2021. During the pause, the team remained together and found innovative ways to continue collaborating and communicating to keep the design process moving forward.

pending_qa.q: What innovative technologies and prefabrication methods are being used in modern hospital construction to improve safety and schedule efficiency?
pending_qa.r: McCarthy is implementing a 3D coordination platform called Revisto, which is similar to Navisworks and allows the team to work in both 3D and 2D combined fashion to identify and resolve design issues quickly. The project utilizes prefabrication of bathroom pods, which are constructed off-site through a joint venture of local trade partners and flown in to site. Trade partners are also prefabricating racks for piping, ductwork, and electrical conduit and bringing them to site just-in-time, reducing the number of materials and workers on site.

pending_qa.q: How is modularization being applied to the facade and enclosure of a 16-story hospital tower?
pending_qa.r: The upper 10 floors of the building, from level 6 to 16, utilize a modularized system called a unitized curtain wall system. Whether the facade is glass or ultra-high-performance concrete panels, all components are mounted to unitized curtain wall frames and then set from a crane interior to the building around the entire enclosure, rather than being assembled on site.

pending_qa.q: What are the diversity and inclusion participation goals for a major healthcare campus construction project?
pending_qa.r: Phase 3 of the BJC project has participation goals of 25% minority-owned and 5% women-owned business enterprises, and also 25% minorities and 5% women for individual workforce participation. McCarthy is encouraging contractors to partner with MWBEs and expects to have 100 to 150 trade partners on the job nested in tiers, which is more than they traditionally would have on a project of this type.

pending_qa.q: How can construction teams support minority and women-owned business enterprises through payment processes and mentorship during large projects?
pending_qa.r: BJC and McCarthy created a dedicated diversity and inclusion functional team with a project-specific inclusion plan (PSIP). The approach includes creative bid packaging to break out smaller scopes of work as exclusive opportunities for smaller subcontractors. McCarthy sends monthly surveys to all trade partners across all tiers to gather feedback and is implementing expedited payment processes for design partners, with a construction plan in development to ensure second and third tier disadvantaged business partners are paid in the same time frame.

pending_qa.q: What workforce scale and contractor participation structure is required for a multi-year hospital tower construction project?
pending_qa.r: The project is expected to have around 300 to 325 workers at peak, which will occur during the 2023 calendar year. Because of the emphasis on diversity and inclusion, there will be 100 to 150 total trade partners on the job, nested in tiers, with McCarthy responsible for ensuring each trade partner—whether first tier or second tier—has the opportunity to succeed on the project.

pending_qa.q: What is the construction timeline and phasing strategy for a 16-story hospital replacement tower?
pending_qa.r: Construction starts in November 2021, with the first patient expected in the tower in summer of 2025, spanning approximately three and a half years. The cast-in-place concrete frame will continue until the third quarter of 2023. As the structure rises, the building skin and enclosure will be constructed from the lower floors upward. Interior fit-out begins once the building becomes enclosed. Construction completion is targeted for the end of 2024.
